advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting is_watchdog_timeout returns True for a CompletedProcess with a non-124 returncode whose stderr contains 'git timed out after' (the documented message fallback).
evidence: src/rebar/_store/git_outcome.py:276-278: `if returncode == WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_RC: return True` then `return bool(returncode) and WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_MARKER in _failure_text(result).lower()`
Docstring at git_outcome.py:269-270 names the fallback explicitly: 'with its message as a fallback for a result that lost that code on the way.'

Named violating input: `subprocess.CompletedProcess(["git","merge"], 1, "", "git timed out after 120s")` must return True via the fallback, but no test asserts this; the parametrized false cases (returncodes 1/128/1/0) all use non-marker text, and the true-case test uses rc 124.
advisory.finding: The documented fallback branch of git_outcome.is_watchdog_timeout — a result carrying the 'git timed out after' marker text but a non-124 returncode ('a result that lost that code on the way') — has no test exercising its TRUE path. The parametrized false-case test only covers non-matching text with non-124 codes and an rc-0 case; the rc-124 test only exercises the first branch. A regression that drops or inverts the marker-text fallback (e.g. `return returncode == WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_RC`) would pass the entire suite.
scenarios: A refactor simplifies is_watchdog_timeout to key only on rc-124, silently dropping the marker fallback; the suite stays green while a result that lost its 124 code is misclassified as a conflict and sends the operator back to fsck-recover.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized true-case: `assert git_outcome.is_watchdog_timeout(subprocess.CompletedProcess(["git","merge"], 1, "", "git timed out after 120s"))`.
